title: Differential effect of supercoiling on bacterial transcription in topological domains.
authors: Goldberg, Boaz; Yehya, Nicolas; Xiao, Jie; Meyer, Sam
one_liner_zh: 该文用数值模拟研究DNA超螺旋对细菌转录的调控，虽涉及DNA拓扑与转录机制，但非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，且方法为随机模拟而非AI或分子动力学，与课题关联较弱。
abstract: DNA supercoiling (SC), the over- and under-winding of DNA, is generated by transcription as described in the twin-domain model. Conversely, SC also impacts transcription through torsional stress. SC therefore regulates transcription dynamically and independently of transcription factor binding, particularly in the context of chromosomal topological domains and the activity of topoisomerases in bacteria. In this work, we develop numerical simulations of SC-coupled transcription of a single gene within a topological domain, based on a model incorporating stochastic transcription and activities of topoisomerase I and gyrase. We explore the effect of several parameters not systematically assessed in previous works (role of topoisomerase activities, topological domain size, gene expression strength) and compare the simulation results to a diverse set of experimental observations ranging from in vitro transcription assays to transcriptomics datasets from various species. This model recapitulates the non-monotonic dependence of transcription in vitro with the superhelical density of the plasmid template. Simulations of in vivo transcription in a closed domain exhibit a qualitatively different role for the two topoisomerases, as well as qualitatively different regulatory behaviors depending on the promoter strength. Specifically, topoisomerase I is required for strongly expressed genes that may be hindered by stalled RNA Polymerase, whereas gyrase activity favors the expression of all genes by enhancing transcription initiation and modulating the burstiness of transcription. The simulations exhibit a new mechanism for transcription bursting mediated by negative SC accumulating at the promoter region and modulating the initiation rate, resulting in levels of burstiness compatible with values reported in cells. Finally, we analyze several transcriptomics datasets from a range of evolutionarily distant species and show that topoisomerase inhibition is systematically associated with the repression of highly expressed genes. Simulations show this behavior to occur within a limited parameter range and thus indicate a biologically relevant regime for the simulations. Overall, this work provides a more quantitative description of how SC contributes to differential gene regulation and transcriptional bursting in bacteria.
abstract_zh: DNA超螺旋（SC），即DNA的过旋和欠旋，由转录产生，如双结构域模型所述。反之，SC也通过扭转应力影响转录。因此，SC独立于转录因子结合，动态调控转录，尤其在染色体拓扑结构域和细菌中拓扑异构酶活性的背景下。在本工作中，我们基于包含随机转录及拓扑异构酶I和旋转酶活性的模型，开发了拓扑结构域内单基因SC耦合转录的数值模拟。我们探讨了先前工作中未系统评估的几个参数的影响（拓扑异构酶活性、拓扑结构域大小、基因表达强度），并将模拟结果与从体外转录实验到多种物种转录组数据集的一系列实验观察进行比较。该模型重现了体外转录对质粒模板超螺旋密度的非单调依赖性。封闭结构域内体内转录的模拟显示，两种拓扑异构酶在功能上存在定性差异，且根据启动子强度表现出定性不同的调控行为。具体而言，拓扑异构酶I对于可能受停滞RNA聚合酶阻碍的强表达基因是必需的，而旋转酶活性通过增强转录起始和调节转录爆发性，有利于所有基因的表达。模拟揭示了一种新的转录爆发机制，该机制由启动子区域积累的负SC介导，调节起始速率，产生的爆发水平与细胞中报道的值相符。最后，我们分析了来自一系列进化上远缘物种的多个转录组数据集，并显示拓扑异构酶抑制与高表达基因的抑制系统性相关。模拟显示，这种行为发生在有限的参数范围内，从而指示了模拟的生物学相关状态。总体而言，本工作提供了SC如何促进细菌中差异基因调控和转录爆发的更定量描述。
